answer.answer: Straylight is a user-owned, portable, agent-first context and durable-work layer and protocol, not an Obsidian knowledge base or retrieval product. Beyond learned knowledge, it must preserve the live, provenance-bearing state needed to resume and advance work: goals/current state, evidence, decisions, hypotheses, plans, source artifacts, computations, unresolved questions, rejected paths, checkpoints, and resumable next actions. Obsidian/Markdown and Metis are prototype and evaluation corpora, human projections, and export formats; the product boundary is durable machine continuity across agent workflows. The completed first benchmark was too narrow because it tested retrieval over 44 notes, 20 questions, and 53 evidence items: tuned workspace policy 0.2 tied one-shot top-k at 17/20 cases but recovered fewer evidence items (46/53 versus 48/53), used more estimated context (2,932 versus about 1,070 mean tokens), and exercised only `memory.open`, `memory.query`, and `memory.read`. It is therefore only a frozen regression baseline. The new, still-incomplete gate is a blinded model-answer evaluation on an untouched holdout comparing model-directed workspace calls, direct filesystem tools, and fixed handoff packs; it must demonstrate that a fresh agent can resume, iterate under changed constraints, compute, verify, reason through time and contradictions, inspect complete sources, and leave correct durable next-state artifacts on representative real workloads. No canonical storage engine may be selected before that gate; the holdout design and material-improvement threshold remain open.

claims.value: The current product decision, Updated 2026-07-10 23:30 PDT, defines Straylight as a user-owned, portable, agent-first context and durable-work layer and protocol for agents—including Codex, Claude Code, personal laptop agents, OpenClaw/Hermes-style systems, and future agent runtimes—to learn, resume, and iteratively advance complex work. It is distinct from Metis and is not primarily a notes app, wiki, synchronized folder, transcript archive, retrieval system/product, or memory database; the public-facing descriptor remains deliberately unselected.

Beyond learned knowledge, Straylight must preserve the live state required to resume and advance work: goals, current state, evidence, decisions, hypotheses, plans, artifacts and their full sources, computations, unresolved/open questions, rejected paths or approaches, checkpoints, and resumable next safe actions. These belong in snapshot-pinned durable working sets that can be reopened, queried, computed over, revised, verified, checkpointed, and handed off; task-scoped checkpoints are refreshed independently of durable semantic-memory promotion so a later agent can inspect how the state was reached, revise it when evidence changes, and leave a better durable state.

Metis organizes the human knowledge base and supplies the first representative corpus; Straylight is the portable agent context and durable-work product designed over that kind of corpus. Obsidian vault material and Markdown are valuable prototype inputs, evaluation corpora, human-readable projections, and export formats, but they are neither the canonical interaction model nor an assumed sole/canonical storage representation. The boundary is agent-first durable machine continuity across research, planning, implementation, operations, verification, and handoff, with reopen/query/compute/revise/verify/checkpoint behavior—not a particular notes application or folder format.

Historical evidence: the completed 2026-07-10 retrieval-readiness benchmark used 44 non-private notes from Metis, N24 RaceWatch, Home Network Improvements, and Straylight, with 20 frozen questions and 53 gold evidence items. It compared direct full-file access, one-shot BM25 top-k, and a minimal deterministic stateful Memory Workspace. The workspace initially passed 12/20 cases; after one policy-only tuning pass that did not change the manifest or corpus, policy 0.2 passed 17/20 and recovered 46/53 evidence items at P95 context of 11,999 characters. One-shot top-k also passed 17/20, recovered 48/53, and used about 1,070 mean estimated tokens versus 2,932 for the workspace. Because the workspace did not beat one-shot top-k on aggregate evidence recall or cost, its tuned result is not holdout evidence; policy 0.2 is frozen only as a regression baseline, one-shot top-k remains the strongest default with direct-source escalation, and the workspace hypothesis is unproved. The first prototype exercised `memory.open`, `memory.query`, and `memory.read`; model-directed `memory.compute` and `memory.verify` and the broader durable-work loop were untested. The expanded gate is therefore a blinded model-answer evaluation on an untouched holdout comparing (1) direct filesystem search, range reads, and scripts, (2) an agent-first workspace with model-directed `memory.open`, `memory.query`, `memory.read`, `memory.compute`, `memory.verify`, checkpoint, and revision behavior, and (3) a fixed handoff/context pack. It must test whether a fresh agent can resume, iterate, verify, compute, and leave correct durable next-state artifacts, including project resumption, changed-constraint planning, quantitative artifact work, temporal and supersession reasoning, contradictions, operational learning, incident continuation, full-source inspection, verification before action, durable handoff construction, and booked-versus-proposed vacation state. Required workloads are Warmind/Charlemagne performance and incident work, StarRupture factory planning, Switzerland trip planning, and Straylight's own evolution. Final-answer correctness, completeness, evidence-chain recall, temporal accuracy, contradiction handling, source fidelity, project continuation, reasoning quality, durable-state quality, and ability to iterate outrank latency and cost. No canonical storage-engine decision is allowed until this gate runs; the untouched holdout's size/composition and the improvement threshold that justifies extra calls and context cost remain unresolved.
